precepts.text: When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord. The apostles, the disciples, when they were come together, they asked of Jesus Christ, saying what? Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? Restore the kingdom to Israel. So Christ's kingdom is Israel's kingdom as well. You all understand that? So we are asking for Christ to bring us the kingdom, because we are joint heirs with him.
precepts.point: Thy kingdom come. So Christ said pray to the Lord for his kingdom to be done on earth. We are joint heirs with him. So what are we actually praying for? We are praying for our kingdom as well.

note.label: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come.” Christ said to pray for the Lord's kingdom to come on earth. We are joint heirs with him, so what are we actually praying for? Our kingdom as well.

“When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The apostles, when they came together, asked Christ to restore the kingdom to Israel. So Christ's kingdom is Israel's kingdom as well. We are asking Christ to bring us the kingdom, because we are joint heirs with him.

We have always wanted to know when it is coming. Ezra asked it: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” When shall be the end of the first world we are subjugated to, in bondage under, and the beginning of our kingdom, where the saints can rejoice in glory? The disciples asked it on the mount of Olives: “Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?” Christ told them to learn the parable of the fig tree: when the branch is tender and puts forth leaves, you know summer is nigh. “So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” When you see the decadence of this society, know that the tribulation and the destruction are near, even at the doors.

And God told Ezra what to watch: “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Jacob's hand held fast Esau's heel for a reason. When Esau goes down, we come up; when Esau is destroyed, we are in our kingdom. That's why the churches don't teach about Esau: the people at the top know, and they make sure it's hidden. So every time you pray thy kingdom come, you are praying for the destruction of the present kingdom. Christ's kingdom is not going to rule beside Babylon the Great; Christ isn't setting a throne beside the president.

precepts.text: While they beheld, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight. Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? This same Jesus shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Christ spake this parable “because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.” A lot of people thought the kingdom was coming at that time. That's why Paul later said, let no man deceive you: that day shall not come except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed.

“A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.” The far country in this context is the heavens. Acts shows him going: “while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.”

And Acts shows him returning: “Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.” The nobleman is Christ. He went into heaven to receive the kingdom, and he is coming back, and when he returns he calls his servants to account.

precepts.text: The husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church.
precepts.point: The husband is the head of the wife, as Christ is the head of the church. There is no glory for the women unless the men have theirs.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
The apostles asked, “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” That is what we want, brothers, and you sisters should want it too. But it is not going to be returned unless the man is in his proper order. The Most High is not going to give the kingdom to the women and not the men; there is no glory for the sisters unless the men get their glory as prophesied.

Some sisters make a face at that and say, I love Jesus directly. So Paul backs it up: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” It is the same thing: there is no salvation except through Christ, and the man is the saviour of the body. The flock of the pasture is men, and the saviours on Mount Zion are men.

Look at the so-called white woman, whom the other women worship, with the Vogue magazines and Miss America. She would have none of that if she did not support her man; the man had to guarantee her sovereignty and her safety so she could prance around. Those women were behind their men a thousand percent, even in evil, going out to the lynchings to support them. Yet that same man keeps his woman in check and tells our women they don't need you brothers. All women expect their men to guarantee their protection; the fact that this must even be addressed among our women is evidence of our destruction.

The charger only has a need because the phone was created. The woman is the charging station, but with no phone you aren't charging nothing. The charger came out of the phone: woman was taken out of man, and she is a helpmate and a comfort to him so he can guarantee her protection and the offspring. You won't get past this brother, because you came from the brother. So the charging stations need to be in full force, and the men have to get in order so the kingdom can be restored.

precepts.text: Christ was taken up and received in a cloud; taken up means received by the Most High.
precepts.point: Enoch walked with God and was not: the Most High took him up, and Enoch did not taste death, the same way Elijah did not taste death.

note.label: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam

precepts.why:
“And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” Christ was taken up and received in a cloud. Taken up means received by the Most High.

So “God took him” is Enoch being taken up and received the same way. He walked with God, and he was not, because the Most High took him up, as Elijah was taken and as Christ was taken.

precepts.text: The apostles cast lots between Joseph called Barsabas and Matthias, and the lot fell upon Matthias; lots were cast without the Urim and Thummim.
precepts.point: Joshua likewise was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; the Most High gave revelation through it.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
One theory holds that the Urim and the Thummim were cast as lots. But the apostles, who were not dealing with the Levitical priesthood, “appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias”, prayed to the Lord “which knowest the hearts of all men” to shew which of the two he had chosen, “And they gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias”.

Lots were cast without any Urim and Thummim, which is an issue with that theory. The better theory is that they served as a symbol of the high priest's authority to seek counsel of the Most High, His will being revealed to him through inner illumination: lights and perfections, a divine discerning beyond a man's own thinking.

precepts.text: The apostles asked if the Most High would at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel, and Christ did not rebuke them but said it is not for them to know the times the Father has put in his own power.
precepts.point: The Most High chooses Israel's inheritance for them; it will not be up to you to say you do not want to rule the nations. The spirit will be put on you and you will be kings, your wives goddesses and queens, your sons princes, your daughters princesses, ruling the whole planet in righteousness.

note.label: Psalm 47: God the Great King Over All the Earth

precepts.why:
Israel ruling the nations is not something Christ did away with. His apostles asked him, “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” Christ did not rebuke them. “It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.”

The kingdom is restored to Israel; only the time is the Father's. So “He shall subdue the people under us, and the nations under our feet” still stands, and every time commandment keepers gather, the Sabbath, the new moon, the feast days, camp 101, the Titus 2 events, it is a time of triumph and rejoicing in the Most High in this wicked world while we wait for that time.

precepts.text: Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? The kingdom was Israel's and was lost for disobedience.
precepts.point: He that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite. Those that remain are the ones who will reverence Israel and serve.

note.label: Zechariah 9: Thy King Cometh Unto Thee, Just and Having Salvation

precepts.why:
“When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The kingdom was Israel's and was lost for disobedience; the disciples knew it was to be restored again to Israel.

The nations named here spoiled that kingdom and are judged for it, and he that remaineth of them shall be for our God, as a governor in Judah and Ekron as a Jebusite: those that remain are the ones who will reverence Israel and serve when the kingdom is restored.

precepts.text: Many took in hand to set forth in order a declaration of the things surely believed, delivered by eyewitnesses and ministers of the word; Luke had perfect understanding of all things from the very first.
precepts.point: Theophilus' name means love of God. He was an Israelite, not a gentile, and Luke addresses him as "most excellent," a title of nobility or government office, the same way Paul addressed "most noble Festus."

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
Luke wrote both the Gospel of Luke and the book of Acts. “The former treatise” is the Gospel of Luke, and it was addressed to the same man: “to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus.” The two books are two letters from the same hand.

“Many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us, Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses, and ministers of the word.” The scriptures we have are a collection of the apostles' teaching passed down to the young men under them, the seventy, and the other disciples. Luke was not one of the twelve, though it is speculated he was of the seventy, and he was there from the beginning, “having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first.” Just as the bishops and elders pass down history to us today so that we can speak on it though we were not there, that knowledge was passed down to Luke.

Theophilus' name means love of God. He was an Israelite, not a gentile, and Luke calls him “most excellent”, a title of nobility or government office, the same way Paul addressed most noble Festus. Luke wrote “That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.”

precepts.text: Paul knew Luke personally and calls him the beloved physician, showing Luke was present throughout the ministry.
precepts.point: Theophilus' name means love of God. He was an Israelite, not a gentile, and Luke addresses him as "most excellent," a title of nobility or government office, the same way Paul addressed "most noble Festus."

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you.”

Paul knew Luke personally and calls him the beloved physician. That shows Luke was present throughout the ministry. He was not one of the twelve, but he was there, and what he wrote of “all that Jesus began both to do and teach” was delivered to him by eyewitnesses and written by a man who walked with the apostles.

precepts.text: Only Luke is with me, take Mark; Luke traveled with Paul, and Mark is the one who wrote the Gospel of Mark.
precepts.point: Theophilus' name means love of God. He was an Israelite, not a gentile, and Luke addresses him as "most excellent," a title of nobility or government office, the same way Paul addressed "most noble Festus."

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.”

Luke traveled with Paul. When others had gone, Luke was still with him. And the Mark Paul calls for is the one who wrote the Gospel of Mark. These were the men under the apostles, the ones the teaching was passed down to, and that is how Luke came to write his former treatise and then the Acts.

precepts.text: Thus it behoved Christ to suffer and rise the third day, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
precepts.point: "All nations" does not mean the Chinese or the Japanese. Prophetically it means the Israelites scattered among all nations: into Assyria (which is why Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled), then Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece, and Rome, then into Africa and out through the transatlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades. That prophecy did not happen only once; it happened all through history.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
Luke gave a full historical account of everything Christ did, from his birth “Until the day in which he was taken up”, and the end of Luke segues straight into Acts. The commandments Christ gave through the Holy Ghost are right there: “Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.”

“All nations” does not mean the Chinese or the Japanese. Prophetically it means the Israelites scattered among all nations: into Assyria, which is why Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled; then Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece and Rome; then into Africa and out through the transatlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades. That prophecy did not happen only once; it happened all through history. Repentance was to be preached to Israel wherever they were scattered.

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.”

This is why the commandment was to preach “among all nations.” The Most High said he would scatter Israel among the nations and leave them few in number among the heathen. That scattering placed our people in every captivity: Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece, Rome, and then out of Africa through the slave trades. The apostles were sent to Israel wherever the Lord had led them.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

That is what “all nations” looks like. These were not gentiles; they were Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, because every nation that ruled over Israel carried them off into exile. So when Christ commanded that repentance be preached “among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem”, it began with Israelites gathered at Jerusalem from every land they had been scattered into.

precepts.text: He was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve, then of above five hundred brethren at once, then of James, then of all the apostles, and last of all of Paul, as one born out of due time.
precepts.point: Within that time he was seen by many. Cephas is another name for Peter and means stone.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
After his passion Christ “shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days.” He did not appear for only a day or two; he stayed forty days, speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of the Most High, to open their understanding further.

Within that time he was seen by many: “he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles.” Cephas is another name for Peter, and it means stone.

“And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.” Paul was the last to see him. Those are the many infallible proofs: Christ alive, seen by hundreds of witnesses.

“Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.” He had to die for the Holy Ghost to be given. That is why they had to wait.

Christ could teach only so much in three years, because a man can bear only so much. The Comforter would open their understanding in increments after his death, guiding them into all truth and bringing his words back to their remembrance. That is the promise of the Father they were told to wait for in Jerusalem.

The order is the same as in Proverbs: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit. precepts.text: John baptized with water unto repentance, but he that came after him would baptize with the Holy Ghost and with fire.

John said it himself: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire.” John's water baptism was always symbolic, a preparation leading up to Christ. Baptism comes from the word baptizo, out of the purification laws.

John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments.

When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly. That means wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind, the part that consumes and filters information.

“But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.” That is why they were to be baptized with the Holy Ghost “not many days hence.” It could not come until he was glorified.

precepts.text: The spirit of man is the candle of the Most High, searching all the inward parts of the belly; the belly is the mind, and the spirit can be put out like a candle.
precepts.point: John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments. Two of John's own disciples heard Christ and followed him, which is why in Acts the disciples were still baptizing with water even though Christ himself baptized not with water but with the Holy Ghost. When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly, meaning wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind that consumes and filters information; but that Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“The spirit of man is the candle of the Lord, searching all the inward parts of the belly.”

The belly is the mind. That is where the rivers of living water flow from, the place where wisdom and understanding are searched out. And the spirit is a candle: it can be put out like a candle.

precepts.text: The Most High dealt to every man the measure of faith, so the disciples' understanding grew in increments.
precepts.point: "Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
Even after all of this they asked, “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” That shows the Holy Ghost was not yet fully given.

It is given in measures: “God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” Every man is dealt a measure of faith that he has to grow in. In Christ there was no measure, but the disciples knew only so much at that time, and their understanding grew in increments.

precepts.text: John sent from prison to ask, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another; he too expected deliverance at that time.
precepts.point: "Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?”

The disciples asked about restoring the kingdom because they thought Rome was the last captivity. John the Baptist thought the same. He sent from prison to ask whether Christ was the one, because he too expected deliverance at that time.

precepts.text: The fourth beast, dreadful and strong with iron teeth, is Rome; the disciples understood the beasts through Rome but not what came after.
precepts.point: "Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces.”

The fourth beast is Rome. The disciples knew Daniel's beasts up to Rome because their fathers had lived through them, so they thought Rome was the last and the kingdom would be restored in their day. But they did not yet understand what came after: the little horn, Babylon the great and America. That fuller understanding was given later to John, to Peter, and now in these last days.

The disciples did not yet understand the seven seals, because only the Lion of the tribe of Judah could open them. The book was not yet opened to them when they asked if the kingdom would be restored at that time. That understanding was given later to John, and now in these last days.

The kingdom could not be restored in the disciples' time. The falling away had to come first and the man of sin be revealed. He could not be openly named under Rome, where you were jailed for sedition, so Paul wrote in allegory. He would be revealed in a land like America, where the freedom to speak allows the man of sin to be identified plainly.

That is why the disciples asked, “wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?”

precepts.text: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved, and these signs follow them that believe: casting out devils, new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking no deadly thing to their hurt, and healing the sick.
precepts.point: Christians misunderstand this power as merely speaking in tongues, but the Bible defines the power of the Holy Ghost by the signs that follow: casting out devils, speaking with new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking any deadly thing unharmed, and laying hands on the sick to recover. Peter was sought to heal by his shadow and Paul by his handkerchief.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you.” Christians misunderstand this power as merely speaking in tongues, but the Bible defines the power of the Holy Ghost by the signs that follow.

“He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned. And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues; They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.”

That is the power the apostles received. Peter was sought to heal by his shadow, and Paul by his handkerchief.

precepts.text: They were all filled with the Holy Ghost and began to speak with other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance; one instance of that power coming to pass.
precepts.point: Christians misunderstand this power as merely speaking in tongues, but the Bible defines the power of the Holy Ghost by the signs that follow: casting out devils, speaking with new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking any deadly thing unharmed, and laying hands on the sick to recover. Peter was sought to heal by his shadow and Paul by his handkerchief.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.”

That is one instance of the power coming to pass, the promise of Acts 1:8 fulfilled. But tongues is only one of the signs. The power of the Holy Ghost is casting out devils, new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking any deadly thing unharmed, and laying hands on the sick to recover. With that power they were witnesses “both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.”

precepts.text: He layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters and maketh the clouds his chariot; the clouds are his chariots.
precepts.point: The kind of chariot that masks itself in a cloud was seen in 2011 over the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, a glowing orb that descended and then shot off at about four thousand miles an hour over one of the most secure no-fly zones in the world, witnessed by thousands and reported internationally.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“While they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” He was taken up in the middle of his speaking, after forty days. That was the exit.

The Most High “maketh the clouds his chariot.” So this was not merely a cloud but a chariot, an instrument of the angels, the same as the moon is an instrument of the armies above. Christ was received up by a chariot, not carried by little white angels in the clouds as the Christian movies depict.

The kind of chariot that masks itself in a cloud was seen in 2011 over the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem: a glowing orb that descended and then shot off at about four thousand miles an hour over one of the most secure no-fly zones in the world, witnessed by thousands and reported internationally.

precepts.text: The twelve are named, listing Simon called Peter, Lebbaeus surnamed Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite.
precepts.point: Judas the brother of James is not Judas Iscariot the traitor. He called himself Jude or Thaddaeus so as not to be associated with the traitor.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
They returned from the mount called Olivet, a sabbath day's journey from Jerusalem, and went up into an upper room where the eleven abode, and their names are listed. The lists differ across the gospels, because the same men go by different names.

Matthew's list: “The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother; Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alpheus, and Lebbeus, whose surname was Thaddeus; Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.”

Simon is also called Peter and Cephas. Simon the Canaanite is the same man as Simon Zelotes in Acts. And Lebbeus, whose surname was Thaddeus, is the same man Acts calls Judas the brother of James.

precepts.text: The same list names Simon called Peter and Judas the brother of James, showing the differing names for the same men.
precepts.point: Judas the brother of James is not Judas Iscariot the traitor. He called himself Jude or Thaddaeus so as not to be associated with the traitor.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
Luke's own list shows the differing names for the same men: “Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew, Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alpheus, and Simon called Zelotes, And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.”

Where Matthew has Simon the Canaanite, Luke has “Simon called Zelotes”; where Matthew has Lebbeus Thaddeus, Luke has “Judas the brother of James.” And Luke keeps Judas the brother of James apart from “Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.” They are not the same man.

precepts.text: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, is the same apostle as Lebbaeus Thaddaeus.
precepts.point: Judas the brother of James is not Judas Iscariot the traitor. He called himself Jude or Thaddaeus so as not to be associated with the traitor.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James.”

Judas the brother of James is the same apostle as Lebbeus Thaddeus, and he is also called Jude. He is not Judas Iscariot the traitor. He called himself Jude, or Thaddeus, so as not to be associated with the traitor.

precepts.text: Simeon hath declared how the Most High first visited the gentiles; that Simeon is Simon Peter.
precepts.point: Judas the brother of James is not Judas Iscariot the traitor. He called himself Jude or Thaddaeus so as not to be associated with the traitor.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.”

That Simeon is Simon Peter. The same man is Simon, Simeon, Peter and Cephas. That is why the lists of the apostles read differently from book to book: the men are the same, known by different names.

precepts.text: His brethren are named as his family members, the brothers who were with them.
precepts.point: "His brethren" are Christ's own brothers. During his ministry they did not believe in him and told him to go show himself openly in Judaea, but after his death and the miracles they came to believe. James the Just, the Lord's brother, became an apostle and was later killed.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.” His brethren are Christ's own brothers, his family: “Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?”

It was not only the men in that upper room. The women also had to learn, and the men always understood that the women learn alongside them. A camp that keeps the women out of the congregation is wrong. Our people came into slavery together and will come out of captivity together.

precepts.text: His brethren told him to depart and show himself to the world, for neither did his brethren believe in him at that time.
precepts.point: "His brethren" are Christ's own brothers. During his ministry they did not believe in him and told him to go show himself openly in Judaea, but after his death and the miracles they came to believe. James the Just, the Lord's brother, became an apostle and was later killed.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
During his ministry his own brothers did not believe in him. “His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judea, that thy disciples also may see the works that thou doest.” They told him, “If thou do these things, shew thyself to the world. For neither did his brethren believe in him.”

But after his death and the miracles they came to believe. That is why the same brethren who doubted him are found in the upper room, continuing with one accord in prayer and supplication.

precepts.text: Paul saw none of the other apostles except James the Lord's brother, who came to believe after Christ's death.
precepts.point: "His brethren" are Christ's own brothers. During his ministry they did not believe in him and told him to go show himself openly in Judaea, but after his death and the miracles they came to believe. James the Just, the Lord's brother, became an apostle and was later killed.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.”

James the Just, the Lord's brother, came to believe after Christ's death. He is one of the brethren in the upper room, and he became an apostle and was later killed. The brother who once did not believe in him became an apostle of him.

precepts.text: The one accord in one place: Peter, James, John, and the rest of the disciples all gathered together in the upper room.
precepts.point: Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover. It is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits, and Israel kept it through every captivity, Assyrian, Babylonian, and Greek.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alpheus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.”

That is the one accord in one place. Peter, James, John and the rest of the disciples were all gathered together in the upper room, keeping the day of Pentecost after Christ had gone up.

precepts.text: Ye shall receive power after the Holy Ghost is come upon you, and be witnesses unto the uttermost parts of the earth; speaking an unlearned language is that power.
precepts.point: They were filled with the wisdom of the Most High to interpret and speak in the different languages of the lands where Israel had been deported, not glossolalia. If Christ commanded them to go teach all nations, they had to be given the power to speak in the tongues of those nations, and these illiterate Galileans spoke perfectly in languages they never learned.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Christ had told them what was coming: “But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.” Speaking a language you never learned is that power.

They were filled with the wisdom of the Most High to interpret and speak in the different languages of the lands where Israel had been deported, not glossolalia. These were illiterate Galileans, and they spoke perfectly in languages they never learned, because they were sent to witness unto the uttermost part of the earth, where the people were.

precepts.text: The disciples ask, "Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?" which defines the restitution: restoring the kingdom to Israel.
precepts.point: To fit the other nations into this as the gentiles who are grafted in, you have to prove they lost something or had something stolen from them. The scriptures show the opposite: the nations are the ones who did the stealing and the hiding, so they are not the gentiles being restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Restitution is the restoration of something lost or stolen to its proper owner, the same word used when land seized from our people is demanded back. The disciples had already defined what is being restored: “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?”

The restitution of all things is the kingdom restored to Israel. Heaven must receive Christ until those times, and we are living the restitution of all things right now, before he comes.

precepts.text: Later Christ gives the order: ye shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, in all Judea, in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth; this is the beginning of the gospel reaching Samaria, but among Jews first.
precepts.point: Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached Christ unto them. Philip was preaching to the Jews who lived in Samaria, not yet to the Gentiles; the Most High moves in order, causing interruptions and persecutions to push his chess pieces and further spread the gospel.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
Later Christ gives the order: “ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.” Jerusalem first, then all Judea, then Samaria, then the uttermost part of the earth.

Philip going down to Samaria is the beginning of the gospel reaching Samaria, but among the Jews first. The persecution was the interruption the Most High used to push his chess pieces from Jerusalem out to the next place in the order.

precepts.text: The disciples ask whether the Most High will at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel.
precepts.point: All was drawn up again into heaven, meaning Israel restored again to its position of rulership.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And all were drawn up again into heaven.” That means Israel restored again to its position of rulership. The sheet was let down from heaven when Israel was cast down into servitude, and drawn up again when Israel is raised up.

The disciples asked for exactly that: “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?”

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why: Just to prove the point. “When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” See that? They thought it was in: will you restore the kingdom to Israel? Now how come the churches don't read that and go, "No, they made a mistake. It's for everybody"? The hell is this?

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why: What does it mean when it says he went into a far country? “And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” So he went into the heavens, to the true tabernacle. That's where Christ went. That's the far country of the nobleman.

The husband is the head of the wife, as Christ is the head of the church. There is no glory for the women unless the men have theirs.

points: Luke wrote both the Gospel of Luke and the book of Acts. The "former treatise" is the Gospel of Luke, which was also addressed to Theophilus, so the two books are two letters from the same hand.

The scriptures we have are a collection of the apostles' teaching passed down to the young men under them, the seventy, and the other disciples. Luke was not one of the twelve, though it is speculated he was of the seventy, and he was there from the beginning. Just as the bishops and elders pass down history to us today so that we can speak on it though we were not there, that knowledge was passed down to Luke.

Theophilus' name means love of God. He was an Israelite, not a gentile, and Luke addresses him as "most excellent," a title of nobility or government office, the same way Paul addressed "most noble Festus."

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

points: Luke gave a full historical account of everything Christ did, from his birth to the day he was taken up, and records that Christ, through the Holy Ghost, gave commandments to the apostles he had chosen.
The end of Luke segues straight into Acts. The commandment was that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

"All nations" does not mean the Chinese or the Japanese. Prophetically it means the Israelites scattered among all nations: into Assyria (which is why Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled), then Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece, and Rome, then into Africa and out through the transatlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades. That prophecy did not happen only once; it happened all through history.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

points: After his passion Christ showed himself alive by many infallible proofs, being seen forty days and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of the Most High. He did not appear for only a day or two; he stayed forty days to open the understanding further.
Within that time he was seen by many. Cephas is another name for Peter and means stone.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

points: The commandment was to not depart from Jerusalem but to wait for the promise of the Father, which is the Holy Ghost, given only after Christ was glorified.

Christ could teach only so much in three years because a man can bear only so much. The Comforter would open their understanding in increments after his death, guiding them into all truth and bringing his words back to their remembrance.

The Holy Ghost comes in an order that begins with the law: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit and opens the understanding. Only the Most High can give the wisdom to interpret this book, which is the most purchased yet least understood book on the earth.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

points: John truly baptized with water, but they would be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence. There is a distinction between what John taught and what Christ brought.

Baptism comes from the word baptizo, out of the purification laws. John was of the tribe of Levi, his father Zacharias a priest and his mother Elizabeth of the daughters of Aaron, so his water baptism was always symbolic, a preparation leading up to Christ.

John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments. Two of John's own disciples heard Christ and followed him, which is why in Acts the disciples were still baptizing with water even though Christ himself baptized not with water but with the Holy Ghost. When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly, meaning wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind that consumes and filters information; but that Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

points: Even after all of this they asked whether he would at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel, which shows the Holy Ghost was not yet fully given. It is given in measures, and every man is dealt a measure of faith that he has to grow in; in Christ there was no measure, but the disciples knew only so much at that time.

They asked because they thought Rome was the last captivity, and John the Baptist thought the same when he sent to ask whether Christ was the one or they should look for another. They knew Daniel's beasts up to Rome because their fathers had lived through them, but they did not yet understand the little horn, Babylon the great and America, or the seven seals that only the Lion of the tribe of Judah could open. That fuller understanding was given later to John, to Peter, and now in these last days.

The falling away had to come first and the man of sin be revealed; he could not be openly named under Rome, where you were jailed for sedition, so Paul wrote in allegory. He would be revealed in a land like America, where the freedom to speak allows the man of sin to be identified plainly.
"Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

points: Christ said it is not for them to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power. Even after his resurrection Christ did not know the time, which disproves the trinity and the idea that Christ is the Father, showing the Son is separate from the Father.
You come to understand the times and seasons as you live through the prophecies and see prophecy become history.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

Christians misunderstand this power as merely speaking in tongues, but the Bible defines the power of the Holy Ghost by the signs that follow: casting out devils, speaking with new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking any deadly thing unharmed, and laying hands on the sick to recover. Peter was sought to heal by his shadow and Paul by his handkerchief.

The Most High maketh the clouds his chariot, so this was not merely a cloud but a chariot, an instrument of the angels, the same as the moon being an instrument of the armies above. Christ was received up by a chariot, not carried by little white angels in the clouds as the Christian movies depict.

The kind of chariot that masks itself in a cloud was seen in 2011 over the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, a glowing orb that descended and then shot off at about four thousand miles an hour over one of the most secure no-fly zones in the world, witnessed by thousands and reported internationally.

points: Two men stood by them in white apparel and asked the men of Galilee why they stood gazing up into heaven, saying this same Jesus shall so come in like manner as they had seen him go.
The same way Christ ascended into what men call outer space is the same way he will descend.

points: They all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brethren.

This was not only the men; the women also had to learn. The men always understood that the women learn alongside them, so a camp that keeps the women out of the congregation is wrong. Our people came into slavery together and will come out of captivity together.

"His brethren" are Christ's own brothers. During his ministry they did not believe in him and told him to go show himself openly in Judaea, but after his death and the miracles they came to believe. James the Just, the Lord's brother, became an apostle and was later killed.
